props.name: density
props.description: Cell padding, not a height scale. `size` is the height scale every other component uses and a table has no intrinsic height — it is whatever its rows make it. Density is the axis a table actually varies on, and its default value is named for what it is rather than for a comfort level: `default` matches `variant`, and a table that wants tighter rows opts in.

props.name: label
props.description: The name of the scroll region.  The viewport is focusable (`tabindex="0"`) because a scrollable region that cannot be reached from the keyboard is unreachable content (WCAG 2.1.1). With a label it also carries `role="group"` and an accessible name; with none it carries no role at all — an unnamed group is noise in the accessibility tree, not structure.

props.name: striped
props.description: Zebra rows: even body rows take the sunken surface.

props.name: variant
props.description: `default` is the stroked, shadowed container; `plain` drops the container chrome for a table sitting inside a `sk-card`.

ai.summary: A styled container for tabular data, which the consumer writes as a real table.
whenToUse: Tabular data where comparison down a column is the point
The same data in a narrow viewport must scroll sideways without breaking the page
The table needs the dense or striped treatment without hand-rolling it
whenNotToUse: It is a read-only summary of a few fields — use a Card
The layout is a grid of unrelated panels — use Cards in a layout primitive
There is one column and no comparison to make — use a list of Text rows
ai.accessibility: The consumer writes the semantics: `<caption>`, `<thead>`, and `<th scope>`. This element adds a scrollable region that is reachable from the keyboard and carries `role="group"` with an accessible name only when `label` is set — a scroll region a keyboard user cannot reach hides its own content. `label` names that region; it is not a substitute for a `<caption>`.
